incubation_period.value: 2 to 8 days; a previously unexposed flock develops cases over 2 to 8 weeks after the virus is introduced

diagnosis.value: Histopathology, PCR, ELISA, immunofluorescent staining, and viral isolation can all be used

treatment_overview.value: No specific treatment; a vaccine can be given during an outbreak to reduce illness and deaths, though it does not prevent latent infection

when_to_call_vet.value: Birds coughing, gasping for breath, or with bloody eye/nose discharge should be seen promptly, since this is one of the most contagious poultry diseases.

summary.value: Gallid herpesvirus 1 causes infectious laryngotracheitis, a highly contagious respiratory disease in chickens and pheasants spread through respiratory droplets and contaminated surfaces. It causes breathing difficulty and airway inflammation, and while a vaccine exists to reduce outbreak severity, there is no cure once a bird is infected.
